skill.name: gjalla-spec-review
skill.description: Reviews software plans and specifications for architecture, security, quality, user experience, and governance gaps before implementation.
skill.summary: Harden a software specification through five focused expert review perspectives.
skill.author: gjalla

security_audit.summary: The sole static finding is a false positive caused by benign wording about reviewing a specification from multiple expert perspectives. The skill contains only review guidance and shows no malicious intent, prompt injection, or operational security behavior.

static_findings.snippet: Your task is to review this spec from multiple expert perspectives to ensure that this spec meets ou

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 11 requests review of a provided specification from multiple expert perspectives. It does not request discovery of system, network, credential, or environment information.

content.value_statement: Ambiguous specifications create implementation gaps, security risks, and costly rework. This skill reviews plans through architecture, security, quality, user, and governance perspectives before engineers begin implementation.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether a proposed design fits existing layers, ownership boundaries, and interaction patterns.
Reviews authentication, authorization, sensitive data handling, input validation, and changing data flows.
Evaluates test strategy, edge cases, integration coverage, and testable acceptance criteria.
Assesses user value, failure behavior, discoverability, and documentation needs.
Separates blocking concerns from recommendations and proposes concrete specification changes.
limitations: The review quality depends on the detail and accuracy of the supplied specification.
The skill does not execute code, tests, scanners, or deployment checks.
Project-specific architecture and governance rules must be provided or available in context.
The review supports expert judgment but does not replace formal security or compliance approval.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Engineering Handoff
use_cases.description: Review a feature specification for missing decisions, unclear acceptance criteria, and implementation risks before assigning development work.

use_cases.title: Strengthen a Technical Design
use_cases.description: Check architecture boundaries, integration patterns, security controls, and testing plans before requesting design approval.

use_cases.title: Validate Product Readiness
use_cases.description: Assess user outcomes, failure handling, discoverability, and documentation requirements before committing a feature to delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Specification Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this specification using the five defined perspectives. List blocking concerns, recommendations, and concrete changes needed before implementation: [paste specification]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first review of a complete feature specification.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Early Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft specification. Identify missing decisions and assumptions, then propose testable acceptance criteria: [paste draft and relevant project context]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a plan needs structure before formal review.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Cross-System Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this cross-system design against these architecture rules. Trace integration, data flow, ownership, security, testing, and governance risks: [design] [rules]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for changes spanning repositories, services, or ownership boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Conduct a Release-Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a final specification review using this project context. Prioritize blockers, explain impact, propose exact revisions, and define verification criteria: [specification] [context]
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before implementation approval for a high-impact change.

output_examples.input: Review a specification that adds an administrative export endpoint without authorization details.
output: Blocking concern: The specification does not define authorization for the administrative export endpoint.
Required change: Name the allowed roles, enforcement point, denied behavior, and audit logging requirements.
Verification: Add positive and negative authorization tests for every supported role.

output_examples.input: Review a design that introduces asynchronous processing but omits failure behavior.
output: Architecture risk: Retry ownership, idempotency, ordering, and dead-letter handling are unspecified.
User risk: The specification does not explain delayed completion or permanent failure.
Recommendation: Define retry limits, status visibility, recovery procedures, and acceptance tests.

output_examples.input: Review a mature specification with complete architecture and security sections.
output_examples.output: Passes: Architecture boundaries and security controls are explicit. Recommendation: Map each acceptance criterion to a named integration or end-to-end test.

best_practices: Provide the complete specification, relevant architecture rules, and known project constraints.
Resolve blocking concerns before using recommendations to improve clarity and maintainability.
Convert every approved revision into measurable acceptance criteria and verification steps.
anti_patterns: Do not request a definitive review from a short summary that omits system context.
Do not treat recommendations as mandatory without considering project priorities and tradeoffs.
Do not accept broad statements such as secure or well tested without measurable criteria.

faq.question: What documents can this skill review?
faq.answer: It can review feature specifications, implementation plans, technical designs, architecture proposals, and related acceptance criteria.

faq.question: Does the skill modify a specification?
faq.answer: It reports passes, risks, blockers, recommendations, and concrete changes. You can then apply the approved revisions.

faq.question: What context produces the best review?
faq.answer: Include system boundaries, architecture rules, security requirements, user goals, integration details, testing expectations, and governance constraints.

faq.question: Can it replace a security assessment?
faq.answer: No. It identifies specification-level security gaps but does not run scanners, inspect deployed controls, or provide formal approval.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: The output separates concerns that block implementation from recommendations that improve quality, clarity, or maintainability.

faq.question: Can it review cross-repository changes?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide the integration contracts, ownership boundaries, architecture context, and expected behavior for each affected repository.
